distinguishing_features: Application to rail-head rolling-contact-fatigue shelling at curve gauge corners rather than gear tooth-root cracking.
Detection by Rayleigh-wave propagation/scattering of acoustic-emission events rather than speed-corrected mesh-stiffness phase demodulation.
Sensor spacing derived from Rayleigh wavelength and a 10-100 kHz band for rail coverage.
Train-pass event-rate thresholding against rail background noise/telemetry.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Detect early subsurface rolling-contact-fatigue crack nucleation in a rail head before visible shelling using available rail-mounted sensing and telemetry.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism is not viable as written because its claimed 0.1 mm subsurface sensitivity, 5 dB/event-rate thresholds, and equivalence of existing vibration sensors/DAQ to AE Rayleigh-wave instrumentation are asserted rather than physically or experimentally supported under noisy train-pass conditions.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Because the closest art already treats high-frequency AE/vibration monitoring as standard early-fatigue detection, applying it to rail RCF with routine Rayleigh-wavelength spacing and baseline thresholds would be an obvious adaptation.
